This pattern aligns closely with climatological August averages and recent model consensus, producing the overwhelming market-implied probability for a daily high of 32 °C. A sudden reduction in cloud cover or a shift in steering flow that suppresses showers could allow additional surface heating and push readings higher, though current observations and short-range guidance make such an outcome unlikely before the close of the observing period.

Northerly winds of 15–25 km/h advect cooler maritime air, keeping temperatures 4–6°C below seasonal averages for late August. Hourly observations through midday show readings climbing from the low 20s into the mid-20s but stalling short of 27°C, while ensemble guidance shows limited upside potential. The market’s heavy weighting toward 24°C (44.5%) and 23°C (32.5%) reflects trader consensus on this suppressed thermal profile, with only modest probability assigned to 25°C (29.5%) if breaks in cloud cover allow brief additional warming. Higher thresholds remain negligible given the persistent synoptic setup and ongoing precipitation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from agencies including the Met Office and ECMWF show Amsterdam’s peak temperature on August 29 likely reaching 21–23 °C under southwesterly flow, high humidity near 70–85 %, and persistent cloud cover with showers that reduce solar insolation. These conditions cap radiative heating while mild maritime air keeps overnight lows near 16–17 °C. Minor differences in timing of heaviest rain or brief clearing explain the near-even market split between 22 °C and 23 °C outcomes; warmer peaks would require stronger insolation or a later shower arrival, while cooler readings depend on earlier or more widespread precipitation. Official observations and updated model runs through the afternoon will resolve the final maximum.

Ongoing high pressure over the Southwest has sustained a regional heat wave, yet the coastal location benefits from southwest winds and a shallow marine layer that advects cooler, moister Pacific air inland during the afternoon. This caps afternoon maxima at the official NOAA LAX station despite sunny skies and highs potentially reaching the mid-90s farther inland. Recent NWS and model guidance consistently show highs in the low-to-mid 80s at LAX under these conditions, aligning with the market's heaviest volume on the 84–85°F bin (53.5% implied probability). Adjacent ranges at 82–83°F and 86–87°F capture residual forecast spread, while probabilities drop sharply outside this narrow window due to the stabilizing influence of the sea breeze and typical late-August climatology. Updated model runs and morning observations have reinforced this consensus without major shifts, keeping trader focus on the 84–85°F threshold as the most likely resolution.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Wuhan indicate a moderating influence from peripheral airflow associated with a typhoon system, bringing increased cloud cover, showers, and northerly winds that limit solar heating after several days of 36–38°C maxima. Updated model runs and local meteorological briefings tomorrow morning will provide the final observational data for market resolution.

**Trader sentiment for Amsterdam's August 30 maximum temperature centers on 21°C as the clear favorite (59% implied probability), followed by 22°C (29%), with 20°C a distant third (8.5%).** These probabilities align closely with short-range forecast guidance issued on August 29, which shows a daytime high near or at 21°C under mostly cloudy to overcast skies with periods of light rain or showers.

A broad low-pressure system and associated frontal boundary are driving the pattern, with southwesterly to westerly flow advecting cooler, moist maritime air from the North Sea. Persistent cloud cover limits surface heating and solar insolation, keeping temperatures near the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 21.1°C. Model consensus (including GFS-derived guidance) points to afternoon peaks around 20–21°C, with only modest diurnal warming before evening cooling.

Recent developments reinforce this outlook: widespread showers and rain on August 29 have maintained a stable, unsettled regime that is expected to continue into August 30 without significant clearing or warmer advection. No strong high-pressure build or subtropical ridge is indicated that would support readings of 23°C or higher, keeping those outcomes at low single-digit probabilities. The tight clustering around 20–22°C reflects both the forecast consensus and the narrow uncertainty range typical for a 24–48-hour European mid-latitude summer forecast.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent monsoon cloud cover, high humidity, and moderate southwest winds are capping daytime heating in Karachi, positioning 30–31°C as the most probable range for the August 30 maximum.** 

Multiple forecast models (GFS ensembles and others) converge on a high near 30–31°C (roughly 86°F) under mostly cloudy to overcast skies, with only low precipitation chances. Recent August observations show typical late-monsoon conditions—haze, 65–90% humidity, and fresh WSW winds of 15–25 mph—that limit solar heating and promote mixing with cooler marine air. Historical August averages hover around 32°C, but the current pattern of persistent cloudiness and sea-breeze influence has kept recent daily highs closer to 29–31°C. 

No heat-wave signals or clearing trends appear in the latest runs, keeping the market-implied odds on 31°C (47.5%) and 30°C (28.5%) well ahead of 32°C (16%). Resolution will hinge on official station readings tomorrow; any unexpected break in cloud cover could push readings higher, though current data favor stability.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent marine layer influence and residual moisture from Saturday’s showers are capping daytime heating in Seattle, keeping the highest temperature on August 30 centered in the upper 60s to low 70s at Sea-Tac Airport.** Official NWS and ensemble guidance point to mostly cloudy skies with limited solar insolation, light winds, and onshore flow that maintains a stable boundary layer and suppresses warming below the late-August climatological average near 75°F. 

Recent model runs converge on afternoon highs near 68–71°F, with the 70–71°F bin edging ahead in trader sentiment because modest afternoon clearing could briefly allow readings in that narrow window, while thicker cloud cover would anchor the peak closer to 68–69°F. The tight spread between these two leading outcomes reflects genuine forecast uncertainty around the timing and extent of any breaks in the overcast rather than a strong warming or cooling signal. Updated guidance through the evening of August 29 will further refine these probabilities ahead of the 24-hour observation window that begins at midnight local time.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and supporting model runs project a daytime maximum of 22°C for London on August 31, supported by a moderate westerly flow advecting cooler Atlantic air and extensive cloud cover that limits solar heating. Scattered light showers or drizzle, expected under 50% probability in afternoon hours, further cap peak values near or slightly below the seasonal average of roughly 20–21°C. Ensemble spread across global models keeps 21–23°C outcomes closely matched, with traders weighting the precise timing of any breaks in cloud and boundary-layer mixing as key variables that could shift the recorded high by 1°C.

These reduce solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling, capping daytime maxima below the late-August climatological average of ~31°C.

Model consensus and HKO guidance show a daytime range of 26–30°C, with high humidity (75–95%) and rain probabilities of 70–80% further limiting heat buildup. A transition toward drier northerly flow begins around September 1, but it arrives too late to meaningfully raise August 31 temperatures. The tight clustering of probabilities around 29–30°C reflects this narrow, rain-suppressed outcome window, while lower odds for 32°C+ or sub-28°C capture residual model spread and any unexpected clearing.

title: Highest temperature in Shanghai on August 31?

**Trader consensus favoring 33°C (53.5% implied probability) for Singapore’s highest temperature on August 31 reflects the Meteorological Service Singapore fortnightly outlook for daily maxima of 33–34°C during the second half of August under prevailing southwest monsoon conditions, with a few days potentially reaching 35°C.**

Afternoon thundery showers remain possible but are not expected to substantially suppress the peak reading at the Changi reference station. Historical climatology places the typical August 31 maximum near 31°C, so the current elevated baseline and official guidance explain why 32°C and 34°C bracket the leading outcomes while lower or higher extremes carry minimal market weight. Updated model runs and the next daily forecast will provide the primary near-term catalyst for any probability shifts.

Updated model runs and official briefings ahead of August 31 will refine the final resolution range.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=katl

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Consensus forecasts from the National Weather Service and major models position Atlanta’s August 31 high in the low 90s.** Mostly sunny skies, light easterly winds around 5 mph, and only a 20% chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms support strong daytime heating under high pressure. Dew points near 71–73°F add humidity without strongly capping temperatures, while the absence of significant cloud cover or frontal activity favors readings near 92°F—well above the late-August climatological average of roughly 85°F. Model agreement remains high through the weekend, though minor shifts in timing of any convection or subtle changes in steering flow could nudge the peak into the 90–91°F or 94–95°F bins. Traders have aligned with this stable forecast consensus, reflected in the leading 92–93°F outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble forecasts show Chicago under strengthening southwesterly flow ahead of mid-level ridging, with Monday’s high most likely falling in the upper 80s to low 90s. Variable morning cloud cover, gusty winds, and a modest chance of afternoon showers introduce meaningful spread across model runs, keeping implied probabilities evenly distributed from 86–95 °F. Official point forecasts sit near 88–90 °F, while historical late-August normals and recent heat-index trends support the potential for brief excursions above 90 °F if skies clear earlier than expected. Updated model guidance and NWS forecast discussions through the weekend remain the key near-term catalysts for any shift in trader positioning.
